Get GPU memory snapshot

Source: R/gpu-memory.R
gpu_memory_state.Rd

Returns the current GPU memory state including total, free, and used memory, and what cuplyr's memory resource holds. Useful for monitoring GPU memory usage during operations.

Usage

gpu_memory_state()

Value

A list with:

available

Logical: TRUE if GPU is available

total_bytes

Total GPU memory in bytes

free_bytes

Free GPU memory in bytes

used_bytes

Used GPU memory in bytes: device level, total - free, for every process on the card. It includes everything the memory resource holds from the device, so freeing a table does not lower it while the resource keeps the memory for reuse (always under "pool"; under "async" until gpu_gc() or an automatic release hands it back, see below). Use pool_used_bytes for what cuplyr's tables occupy.

total_gb

Total GPU memory in gigabytes

free_gb

Free GPU memory in gigabytes

used_gb

Used GPU memory in gigabytes

resource

"async" (the default), "pool" or "cuda": the RMM memory resource cuplyr installed at load time (see below). "cuda" means none: every allocation is a plain cudaMalloc.

pool_bytes

Bytes the resource currently holds from the device. Under "pool" that is the pool's size; under "async" it is the async pool's reserved memory (cudaMemPoolAttrReservedMemCurrent), which shrinks when memory is returned. NA when resource is "cuda".

pool_used_bytes

Bytes currently allocated from the resource to live columns and scratch space: what cuplyr is using, as opposed to what it reserved. It rises when a table is created and falls when the table is garbage collected. Exact under both resources. NA when resource is "cuda".

The memory resource

Loading cuplyr installs an RMM memory resource as the current device resource, so the many short-lived columns a pipeline allocates are carved out of memory reserved once instead of going through cudaMalloc/cudaFree each time. There are three resources:

"async" (default)

RMM's cuda_async_memory_resource, CUDA's stream-ordered allocator (cudaMallocAsync). By default it keeps freed memory cached for reuse, as the pool does, and runs at the same speed (measured, see the vignette). Unlike the pool it can give the memory back: gpu_gc() synchronises the device and returns everything the pool holds unused, so other processes on the card can use it. With the opt-in cuplyr.release_threshold (below) CUDA also returns unused memory by itself, at the next synchronisation, while the pool's whole reservation is above that threshold. The reservation counts tables in use, so a session that holds more than the threshold keeps nothing cached and allocates from the driver again, at about plain cudaMalloc speed.

"pool"

RMM's pool_memory_resource. Same speed as async by default, but it keeps the high-water mark of its size until the R session ends, so the card's free memory (free_bytes) stays lower than the data you hold; use pool_used_bytes for the latter. gpu_gc() cannot shrink it (released_bytes is 0).

"cuda"

No resource (cuplyr.memory_pool = FALSE, or cuplyr.memory_resource = "cuda"): plain cudaMalloc/cudaFree for every allocation. Slowest per allocation; device free memory is always the truth, and pool_bytes and pool_used_bytes are NA.

Synchronisations happen at collect(), print() and gpu_sync(), and also inside many libcudf calls (for example whenever one copies a size or count back to the host), so an automatic release can happen in the middle of a pipeline. See vignette("memory", package = "cuplyr") for measurements and advice on choosing.

The resource is chosen when the package loads, from options (which win) or environment variables. There is one resource per R process: the switches are read by the first load that creates it, and loading the package again in the same session (pkgload::load_all(), or a reload after unloading) reuses that resource, whatever the switches say then, and reports it; such a load does not read the switches, so it does not warn about them either. Restart R to change them.

Where the GPU or driver does not support cudaMallocAsync, the async resource cannot be created. If async was the default (nothing chosen, or an unknown kind), cuplyr then installs "pool" and gives a warning saying so. If "async" was asked for by name, the warning says the resource could not be installed and nothing is (resource is "cuda").

cuplyr.memory_pool / CUPLYR_MEMORY_POOL

FALSE, or "0", "false", "no", "off", installs nothing (resource is "cuda", the behaviour before the pool existed) unless an earlier load in the session already created the resource. Anything else, or unset (a zero-length or NA option counts as unset), installs the resource.

cuplyr.memory_resource / CUPLYR_MEMORY_RESOURCE

"async" (default) or "pool" to pick the kind of resource; "cuda" or "none" install nothing, like cuplyr.memory_pool = FALSE. Case and surrounding blanks do not matter. Unset or empty means async. Any other value gives a warning naming the option or variable and the value as typed, and async is used; when cuplyr.memory_pool switches the resource off, the warning says the value is ignored and no resource ("cuda") is used.

cuplyr.pool_initial / CUPLYR_POOL_INITIAL

How much the resource reserves at load, in bytes, so the first calls need no driver allocation. Default: a quarter of the free device memory, at most 1 GiB. A larger request is clamped to 90 percent of the free memory. 0 reserves nothing up front. Both "pool" and "async" grow by themselves when needed; this is not a limit and not a release threshold.

cuplyr.release_threshold / CUPLYR_RELEASE_THRESHOLD

Async only, opt-in, in bytes; unset (the default) means no automatic release. It is CUDA's release threshold for the async pool: at a synchronisation CUDA returns unused memory to the device until the pool's whole reservation, memory in use included, is at or below it. 0 keeps nothing, the "share the card" setting. The price is speed: while the session holds more than the threshold, every allocation goes to the driver. A zero-length, NA or empty option counts as unset (the environment variable decides). Any other value that is not a non-negative number gives a warning naming the option or variable, and means unset. Ignored under "pool" and "cuda".

All cuplyr options, and how an invalid value is handled, are listed on cuplyr-options.

See also

gpu_details for device information (device level only), gpu_memory_usage for per-object memory estimates, cuplyr-options for the options

Examples

if (has_gpu()) {
  # Check memory before allocation
  before <- gpu_memory_state()

  # Allocate some GPU data
  gpu_df <- tbl_gpu(data.frame(x = runif(1000000)))

  # Check memory after allocation
  after <- gpu_memory_state()

  cat("Memory used:", after$used_gb - before$used_gb, "GB\n")
  cat("Allocated from the resource:",
      after$pool_used_bytes - before$pool_used_bytes, "bytes\n")
}
#> Memory used: 0 GB
#> Allocated from the resource: 8e+06 bytes
